breaking_news.headline: When students attend these colleges, taxpayers often pay. Here's why
breaking_news.summary: Federal data shows many borrowers who aren't paying their loans went to private, for-profit colleges — schools that often market to low-income students and rely on federal financial aid for revenue.

breaking_news.headline: How are rising prices affecting you? NPR wants to know
breaking_news.summary: Inflation, gasoline prices and the cost of living are top of mind in the election season. How are higher costs shaping the way you live? NPR wants to hear.

breaking_news.headline: How Jared Kushner is mixing U.S. diplomacy with his billion-dollar business
breaking_news.summary: The New Yorker's Dexter Filkins says while Trump's son-in-law is a U.S. special envoy negotiating peace, he's also working on private business deals, raising billions in some of the same countries.

breaking_news.headline: A bad year for the crypto industry just got a lot worse
breaking_news.summary: The cryptocurrency industry just suffered a major defeat in a bill they had badly wanted to get through the Senate. It's the latest setback in a terrible year for the sector.

breaking_news.headline: Could trees developed with gene-editing technology protect Florida's citrus industry?
breaking_news.summary: A bacterial infection is wiping out Florida's citrus trees. Growers hope a rootstock developed with gene-editing technology could keep the disease at bay.

breaking_news.headline: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman
breaking_news.summary: Warren Buffett is stepping down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway after serving in the role for more than 50 years. His son, Howard, will become Berkshire Hathaway's new chairman

breaking_news.headline: Ms. Rachel has entered her album era, and she is so happy about it
breaking_news.summary: Ms. Rachel has conquered YouTube, Netflix and the toy aisle. Now she's making an album, with real instruments, big feelings and her littlest listeners in mind.

breaking_news.headline: What expensive sulfur means for your dinner table
breaking_news.summary: Oil supplies are falling, sulfur prices are threatening food costs, and we measure Lego against Hollywood

breaking_news.headline: Dozens of suspected illegal miners die in Nigerian custody
breaking_news.summary: Authorities linked the deaths to disease, but this has been disputed by intelligence reports and relatives of the accused.

breaking_news.headline: Ronaldo named in first Portugal squad since World Cup - at age of 41
breaking_news.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo is named in the first squad selected by new Portugal coach Jorge Jesus for their upcoming Nations League games.

breaking_news.headline: New wild cat species discovered - with only one known living member
breaking_news.summary: A spotted wildcat long mistaken for relatives has been identified as a new species in Bolivia.

breaking_news.headline: At least 21 killed after vehicle loaded with explosives rams Pakistan mosque
breaking_news.summary: A four-year-old child is among those killed in the attack, during which gunmen also opened fire on a police facility.

breaking_news.headline: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror says he had no doubt she deliberately killed her children
breaking_news.summary: It is the first time the juror, who refused to side with the others and acquit Clancy, has spoken publicly about his decision.

breaking_news.headline: Police begin operation to move migrants from Ceuta beaches
breaking_news.summary: Police reportedly fired into the air on Friday morning as they struggled to contain crowds jostling to secure a place at the tented site.

breaking_news.headline: Three dead and eight injured in Philippines school shooting
breaking_news.summary: The gunman is among the dead in what is the third school shooting in the country since June.

breaking_news.headline: Russian hybrid attacks against Europe intensifying, says Macron
breaking_news.summary: The French president says he has tasked the government with protecting critical infrastructure and defence industry sites.

breaking_news.headline: 'Insufficient funds' to pay Brewdog creditors after takeover deal
breaking_news.summary: Administrators say about £489,000 was owed for staff wages and holiday pay and £2.4m was owed to HMRC for unpaid VAT.

breaking_news.headline: Thames Water rescue deal should be rejected - MPs
breaking_news.summary: A report on the future of Thames Water, urging the government to take action, has been published.

breaking_news.headline: The virtual worlds where robots are trained
breaking_news.summary: Training systems that allow robots to negotiate the real world are getting more sophisticated.

breaking_news.headline: British Steel plan lacks credibility, MPs say
breaking_news.summary: A committee report says the government has not set out how British Steel will become profitable.
